correctness.rationale: For 0<t_i<1 on a matching, every vertex of the dual Lip_0 polytope has connected tight-constraint graph (rank of signed incidence normals equals n-1). Because the k short edges alone cannot connect n≥3 vertices, a tight unit edge forces global range 1; all singleton values are anchors 0 or 1 and each short pair must take exactly one of six lower/upper short-tight states. Both group polarities are necessary and sufficient for a connected tight graph, with an all-to-all tight 0–1 anchor core. Therefore precisely 6^k*2^(n−2k)−2*3^k=3^k(2^(n−k)−2) dual vertices, hence primal facets by polarity. A separately written integer potential enumerator independently counted all vertices for every n=3..6 and k≤floor(n/2), using short lengths 2/6,3/6,4/6. This is corroboration; proof covers all real 0<t_i<1.
